text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — canary/embeddings-service: sudden quality drift detected (cosine_distance > 0.5 threshold) at 09:32 UTC. Paging oncall @alex.

alex: on it. getting context — is this across all regions or just canary?

samir: looks limited to canary shard (us-west-2-c2). spike started right after the 09:20 canary roll.

maria: confirmed. commit 8f3b2d1 (quant-embed-adjust) was included in that canary only.

alex: ok. priority is to stop further customer impact — flipping canary flag now.

chris: command to flip (internal flag service):
```
POST https://flags.internal/v1/flags/embeddings_canary/switch
{
  "env": "prod",
  "value": "off",
  "actor": "alex"
}
```

alex: ran the flip at 09:38 UTC — response 200. rolling traffic off canary.

maria: telemetry shows canary request volume dropping; quality metrics trending back to baseline.

samir: initial customer impact: ~0.3% of traffic got degraded responses for ~16 mins, mostly low-volume webhooks. No major customer-facing errors reported yet.

alex: good. next step — decide between quick revert of single commit vs hotpatch. can we hotpatch the quant change?

chris: hotpatch could take longer and risk regressions. single-commit revert on canary is fastest to validate rollback path. I can prepare revert PR and do a canary-only deploy.

maria: +1. keep prod stable; don't promote until we validate.

alex: do it. chris, post the PR link once ready so I can approve and run canary rollout.

chris: creating revert PR now. branch: revert/8f3b2d1. commands I used:
```
git checkout -b revert/8f3b2d1
git revert --no-edit 8f3b2d1
git push origin revert/8f3b2d1
```

chris: PR created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/embeddings/pulls/4123 — requesting review from @maria and @alex.

alex: reviewing now. once green, I'll trigger canary deploy to confirm metrics.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: new canary deployment queued by alex — reverting commit 8f3b2d1 to canary at 09:50 UTC.

maria: CI green. approving PR.

alex: deployed revert to canary at 09:56 UTC. watching metrics.

samir: metrics show quality back within normal window by 09:58 UTC. latency also normalized.

alex: thanks. I'll hold promotion to production until we run a 30m observation window. if stable, we'll roll forward and then plan a full release with more validation.

chris: noted — I'll also add a regression test for cosine_distance distribution to CI. small snippet to add to tests:
```
assert np.percentile(distances, 95) < 0.4
```

maria: logging customer-impacted request IDs for outreach if needed. low severity but keep an eye.

alex: handing over to the morning oncall. Handoff notes:
- Incident: canary embedding quality drift after canary roll (commit 8f3b2d1)
- Action taken: flipped canary flag, reverted commit on canary, validated metrics returning to baseline
- Current state: canary stable, no prod promotion pending 30m gate
- Follow-ups: add regression test, consider more conservative quantization thresholds, review rollout automation to avoid simultaneous canary batches

alex: @maria @chris please join the morning RCA if we see recurrence. leaving page open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident marked MONITORED. Pager oncall changed to morning-oncall at 10:05 UTC.
